# Ready — Style Reference

> Flecked oatmeal paper under floating app windows, one violet cursor flag. Heavy geometric bold over a speckled warm canvas, soft 40px offset shadows instead of lines, and a single amethyst name-tag cursor as the only accent that moves.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Ready speaks a speckled-paper multiplayer language: a warm off-white canvas #f5f4f1 with a visible paper grain carries floating product windows on #ffffff, with all running text in #333333 and secondary captions in #8b8c96. The interface chromatic budget is exactly one hue, an indigo stepping from #5c6ae4 text to #7366fe fill to a #5c6ae433 hairline. It appears as an eyebrow, a highlighter swipe and a collaborator's cursor flag, not as a button, because the measured page ships zero button elements. Six dusk tones from #55269c to #6c77b0 are decorative gradient pigment confined to feature panels and meeting headers. Typography splits the labour sharply: GT Walsheim 700 at 56 and 64px with 1.0 leading carries every headline, while GT America Standard at 300, 400 and 500 handles everything from 14 to 24px, a 2.33× cliff between subheading and display where a conventional Major Third ladder would step gently. Corners round to 24 and 32px, and elevation comes from one directional 11px 11px 40px shadow at 10% black. The page reads as a shared document someone is already editing rather than a sales page asking for a click.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linen Canvas | `#f5f4f1` | `--color-linen-canvas` | The body background under every section, the nav and the hero — a warm oat that lets white product windows float without a single border. |
| Paper | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper` | Product window bodies, meeting card content areas and reversed text on gradient panels (13 text uses) — the only true white, reserved for things that are the product. |
| Graphite Ink | `#333333` | `--color-graphite-ink` | Every headline, body paragraph and table figure (14 uses, the most frequent text color) — a softened black that keeps Walsheim 700 dense without going harsh on warm paper. |
| Pewter Caption | `#8b8c96` | `--color-pewter-caption` | Meeting timestamps, recurrence notes and muted in-product metadata (2 uses) — a cool grey that sits clearly behind Graphite Ink. Do not use it for body paragraphs. |
| Lapis Signal | `#5c6ae4` | `--color-lapis-signal` | The uppercase hero eyebrow, the selected calendar date and checked task boxes (4 uses) — the readable, text-weight form of the single accent hue. |
| Lapis Hairline | `#5c6ae433` | `--color-lapis-hairline` | 1px borders on in-product tables, toolbar chips and the nav rule (4 uses) — indigo at 20% so even dividers carry a trace of the brand hue. |
| Amethyst Cursor | `#7366fe` | `--color-amethyst-cursor` | The "Febby" collaborator name tag, its caret and the hero highlighter swipe at reduced opacity (2 fills) — the signature accent object. Do not promote it to a large section background. |
| Slate Dusk | `#6c77b0` | `--color-slate-dusk` | The cool blue corner of the Automated Templates and Powerful Tools gradient panels — decorative pigment only, the anchor stop of the feature gradients. |
| Lilac Mist | `#817da6` | `--color-lilac-mist` | Mid-stops where blue gradient corners melt toward warm ones on feature panels — decorative-only, softens the transition so the gradients read as weather rather than stripes. |
| Steel Haze | `#6873a5` | `--color-steel-haze` | Secondary blue stop in feature panel gradients and the Team Sync header — decorative-only. Do not use it as a text or border color. |
| Plum Ember | `#8f4d75` | `--color-plum-ember` | Warm rose mid-tone in the Team Meeting header and feature-panel blends — decorative-only, the bridge from violet to the orange corners. |
| Orchid Glow | `#7b4096` | `--color-orchid-glow` | Upper stop of the hero product window header gradient — decorative-only, gives the main mockup its purple crown. |
| Grape Ink | `#55269c` | `--color-grape-ink` | Darkest stop of the hero window header behind white tab labels — decorative-only, the deepest color on the page and the only one dark enough to hold #ffffff text at 14px. |

## Tokens — Typography

### GT Walsheim — the heavy geometric voice of every headline, nothing else · `--font-gt-walsheim`

- **Substitute:** Outfit at 700, Figtree at 800, Plus Jakarta Sans at 800. GT Walsheim Bold draws heavier than its nominal 700 because of its round bowls and short ascenders, so Figtree and Jakarta need one step up to match the stroke mass, and Outfit at 700 lands on it directly.
- **Weights:** 700
- **Sizes:** 56px, 64px
- **Line height:** 1.0
- **Letter spacing:** 0px at 56px, 0px at 64px
- **Role:** Walsheim appears at exactly one weight and two sizes across 7 uses — a display-only face that does not step down into subheads, which is anti-convention for a two-family system. The 1.0 leading packs two- and three-line headlines into dense, friendly blocks, and the geometric single-storey forms soften the bold weight into something closer to a children's book cover than a SaaS banner. The 64/56 ratio is 1.143, almost flat: H1 and H2 are the same voice at nearly the same volume.

### GT America Standard — the neutral grotesk for paragraphs, card titles and UI labels · `--font-gt-america-standard`

- **Substitute:** Inter at 400 (body) and 500 (titles), Public Sans at 400, Instrument Sans at 400. GT America Light 300 renders closer to 350 at 14px, so use Inter at 350 for the light caption rather than 300, which draws noticeably thinner.
- **Weights:** 300, 400, 500
- **Sizes:** 14px, 16px, 18px, 24px
- **Line height:** 1.25, 1.33, 1.43, 1.5
- **Letter spacing:** 0px at 14px, 0px at 16px, 0px at 18px, 0px at 24px
- **Role:** America is the workhorse with 26 uses, carrying everything below the headlines. Its 16→18→24 run steps at 1.125 then 1.333, a Perfect Fourth at the top, and then the scale jumps 2.33× straight to Walsheim — there is no 32 or 40px tier, which is the deliberate cliff that makes headlines feel like a different medium. Zero tracking at every size and a medium 500 ceiling keep the text register conversational; hierarchy below the headline is carried by size and color, not by bolding.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | GT America Standard | 300 | 14px | 1.43 | 0px | `--text-small` |
| caption | GT America Standard | 400 | 14px | 1.43 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body | GT America Standard | 400 | 16px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | GT America Standard | 400 | 18px | 1.33 | 0px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | GT America Standard | 500 | 24px | 1.25 | 0px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-lg | GT Walsheim | 700 | 56px | 1.0 | 0px | `--text-heading-lg` |
| display | GT Walsheim | 700 | 64px | 1.0 | 0px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline in GT Walsheim 700 at 56px or 64px with 1.0 line height — the density of the bold geometric block is the whole display voice.
- Keep the canvas #f5f4f1 with a fine paper grain and float #ffffff product windows on it — tonal contrast plus shadow replaces borders around major containers.
- Ration indigo to text (#5c6ae4), cursor fill (#7366fe) and 20% hairline (#5c6ae433) — one hue at three intensities is non-negotiable for interface color.
- Express the accent as a collaborator: a #7366fe name tag with 8px 8px 8px 0px radius pinned to a 2px caret — the brand's accent is a person, not a button.
- Use the single 11px 11px 40px shadow at 10% black on every floating card — a consistent light source from upper-left makes the stack read as physical paper.
- Jump directly from 24px subheadings to 56px headlines — the 2.33× cliff keeps headlines feeling like a different medium from UI text.
- Confine the dusk gradient palette (#55269c through #6c77b0) to 32px-radius feature panels and 24px meeting headers — saturated area lives only inside containers.

### Don't

- Don't add a filled #7366fe button to the nav — the avatar stack replaces the CTA, and a button turns the collaborator accent back into a sales prompt.
- Don't step headlines down into a 32px or 40px Walsheim tier — Walsheim appears at 700 only, and intermediate sizes blur the cliff between display and UI.
- Don't draw 1px #333333 borders around product windows — the system separates layers with #ffffff on #f5f4f1 and a 40px blur, and ink outlines make it a wireframe.
- Don't flood a full-width section with #55269c or #7b4096 — those stops are gradient pigment, and a dark band breaks the warm-paper continuity of the canvas.
- Don't track the 14px eyebrow wider than 0px or bold it past 400 — the uppercase #5c6ae4 already flags it, and extra weight makes it shout over the 64px headline.
- Don't center the shadow at 0px 0px on cards — the 11px 11px offset is the directional signature, and centered glows flatten the paper-on-desk metaphor.
- Never let indigo fill more area than a tag, a checkbox or a selected date — the thesis is an accent that behaves like a cursor, and a large indigo surface erases it.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #f5f4f1 (Linen Canvas)
- elevated surface: #ffffff (Paper)
- primary text: #333333 (Graphite Ink)
- secondary text: #8b8c96 (Pewter Caption)
- accent text: #5c6ae4 (Lapis Signal)
- border: #5c6ae433 (Lapis Hairline)
- primary action: #7366fe (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Charts and tables stay neutral — #333333 figures on #ffffff with 1px #5c6ae433 dividers and #8b8c96 for comparison series — and only the single highlighted value or bar takes a solid #5c6ae4 fill, so data never outshouts the cursor accent.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button: background #7366fe, text #ffffff, no border, border-radius 8px, padding 10px 20px, height 40px, font GT America Standard (fallback Inter at 500) 16px weight 500, line height 1.5, letter-spacing 0px, no shadow. On hover, keep the same fill and add the `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) 11px 11px 40px 0px` shadow. Place at most one per viewport, and pair it with a secondary button that is transparent with a 1px #5c6ae433 border, #333333 text at 16px weight 400 and the same 8px radius.

2. Build a hero section: page background #f5f4f1 with a subtle grain texture, 1280px centered container, 128px top padding. Center an uppercase eyebrow "YOUR NEW CALENDAR" in GT America Standard 14px weight 400, color #5c6ae4, letter-spacing 0px, 16px below it a two-line headline in GT Walsheim (fallback Outfit 700) 64px weight 700, line height 1.0, color #333333. Highlight the last three words with a #7366fe swipe at 25% opacity, ending in a 2px #7366fe caret and a name tag (#7366fe fill, #ffffff 14px weight 400, padding 4px 8px, radius 8px 8px 8px 0px). Below, 24px gap, an 18px weight 400 paragraph in #333333 with 1.33 line height, then 80px gap and a #ffffff product window with 24px radius and shadow `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2) 0px 1px 128px 0px`.

3. Build a gradient feature panel: border-radius 32px, padding 48px, background a soft radial blend of #6c77b0 at top-left, #817da6 in the middle and #8f4d75 toward a warm orange bottom-right corner, with a fine noise overlay. Title in GT America Standard 24px weight 500, line height 1.25, color #ffffff, then 12px gap and body at 16px weight 400, line height 1.5, color #ffffff. Inset a product popover that bleeds off the bottom edge, and apply shadow `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) 11px 11px 40px 0px` to the panel.

4. Build a meeting card for a horizontal carousel: #ffffff body, border-radius 24px, shadow `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) 11px 11px 40px 0px`. A header band filled with a diagonal gradient from #6873a5 to #8f4d75 holds a #ffffff title in GT America Standard 24px weight 500 and #ffffff metadata at 14px weight 300, padding 24px. Below, an "Agenda" label at 16px weight 500 in #333333, a 1px #5c6ae433 divider, and checklist rows at 16px weight 400 with 8px gaps, checked boxes filled #5c6ae4. Space cards 24px apart and let the row bleed off both viewport edges.

5. Build a navigation bar: sticky, transparent over #f5f4f1, height 48px, 1px #5c6ae433 bottom border, content in a 1280px container. Left: the wordmark "Ready" in GT Walsheim 700 at 24px, color #333333. Right: five 32px circular avatars with border-radius 32px, overlapping by 8px, each with a 2px #ffffff ring. No links and no filled button.

| buttons | 8px |
| smallElements | 0px 0px 8px 8px |

### Layout

- **Card padding:** 48px (32–48px)

## Components

### Sticky Navigation Bar

**Role:** Persistent brand strip, no menu.

Transparent over #f5f4f1, 48px tall, sticky, with a 1px #5c6ae433 bottom rule, the Ready wordmark SVG at left inside the 1280px container and a five-avatar collaborator stack at right, no links, no sign-up button, no shadow; the single measured anchor carries GT America Standard 14px at 400. Against the convention of a five-link nav plus a filled CTA, it shows who is in the room instead of where to click — presence replaces navigation.

### Primary Button — Amethyst Fill (Reconstruction)

**Role:** The single filled call to action.

Absent on the measured page. Zero button elements were extracted, so this spec is reconstructed from the only filled accent object: background #7366fe, text #ffffff, no border, border-radius 8px, padding 10px 20px, height 40px, GT America Standard 16px at 500, no shadow. Use it once per view at most — the system outlier by definition, since the site's thesis is that indigo belongs to collaborators, and a filled button should feel like one more cursor, not a banner.

### Secondary Button — Hairline Ghost

**Role:** Toolbar and template-picker actions.

Quiet, outlined chip. Taken from the in-product "Today" and "Pick a Template" controls: background transparent, text #333333, border 1px #5c6ae433, border-radius 8px, padding 10px 20px, height 40px, GT America Standard 16px at 400, no shadow. It sits on #ffffff or #f5f4f1 without changing either surface — the default for any action that is not the page's single most important one.

### Hero Product Window — Main Content Card

**Role:** The product as hero image.

The page's centerpiece. A #ffffff window with border-radius 24px and the deepest shadow on the site, `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2) 0px 1px 128px 0px`, crowned by a header band blending #7b4096 into #55269c that holds #ffffff tab labels at 14px 400, body content in #333333 at 16px 400, tables bordered in 1px #5c6ae433, padding 48px. Two muted sibling windows flank it on #f5f4f1 at 24px radius — the main card is a real interface, not an illustration of one.

### Meeting Card — Gradient Header

**Role:** Horizontal carousel of meeting examples.

Gradient-crowned document tiles. Each card is #ffffff with border-radius 24px, shadow `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) 11px 11px 40px 0px`, a header band in a two-stop decorative gradient drawn from the dusk palette (#6873a5, #8f4d75, #7b4096), a #ffffff title in GT America Standard 24px at 500, #ffffff metadata at 14px 300, and agenda content below in #333333 at 16px 400 with 24px padding. The bleed off both page edges says the list continues — personality comes from the header color, structure stays identical.

### Gradient Feature Panel

**Role:** Feature explanation with embedded UI.

Weather-map color fields. Border-radius 32px, padding 48px, background a soft multi-stop blend of #6c77b0, #817da6 and #8f4d75 into orange corners (orange is decorative, not a system token), grain overlay, title #ffffff in GT America Standard 24px at 500, body #ffffff at 16px 400 with 1.5 leading, shadow `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) 11px 11px 40px 0px`. Panels stagger in an asymmetric bento with overlapping product popovers — the only place saturated color is allowed to fill area.

### Eyebrow Label

**Role:** Section kicker above headlines.

A whispered caption. "YOUR NEW CALENDAR" in GT America Standard 14px at 400, uppercase, color #5c6ae4, centered, 16px above a 64px Walsheim display line, no background, no border, letter-spacing 0px as measured. The capitals and the accent hue do the work convention assigns to heavy tracking — it is the first appearance of the accent and sets its rationed volume.

### Collaborator Cursor Tag

**Role:** The signature accent object.

A name flag on a live caret. Background #7366fe, text #ffffff, GT America Standard 14px at 400, padding 4px 8px, border-radius 8px 8px 8px 0px, attached to a 2px-wide #7366fe caret running the full 64px height of the headline line, no shadow. The squared bottom-left corner is the deliberate system outlier — it breaks the all-round shape rule so the tag points to its caret like a speech bubble, which is why the exception is allowed.

### Highlighted Headline Phrase

**Role:** Multiplayer selection inside display type.

Text being edited. The words "need to meet" in GT Walsheim 64px at 700, color #333333, sit on a #7366fe swipe at 25% opacity with 0px radius and 4px horizontal overhang, terminated by the Collaborator Cursor Tag. ## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline in GT Walsheim 700 at 56px or 64px with 1.0 line height — the density of the bold geometric block is the whole display voice.
- Keep the canvas #f5f4f1 with a fine paper grain and float #ffffff product windows on it — tonal contrast plus shadow replaces borders around major containers.
- Ration indigo to text (#5c6ae4), cursor fill (#7366fe) and 20% hairline (#5c6ae433) — one hue at three intensities is non-negotiable for interface color.
- Express the accent as a collaborator: a #7366fe name tag with 8px 8px 8px 0px radius pinned to a 2px caret — the brand's accent is a person, not a button.
- Use the single 11px 11px 40px shadow at 10% black on every floating card — a consistent light source from upper-left makes the stack read as physical paper.
- Jump directly from 24px subheadings to 56px headlines — the 2.33× cliff keeps headlines feeling like a different medium from UI text.
- Confine the dusk gradient palette (#55269c through #6c77b0) to 32px-radius feature panels and 24px meeting headers — saturated area lives only inside containers.

### Don't

- Don't add a filled #7366fe button to the nav — the avatar stack replaces the CTA, and a button turns the collaborator accent back into a sales prompt.
- Don't step headlines down into a 32px or 40px Walsheim tier — Walsheim appears at 700 only, and intermediate sizes blur the cliff between display and UI.
- Don't draw 1px #333333 borders around product windows — the system separates layers with #ffffff on #f5f4f1 and a 40px blur, and ink outlines make it a wireframe.
- Don't flood a full-width section with #55269c or #7b4096 — those stops are gradient pigment, and a dark band breaks the warm-paper continuity of the canvas.
- Don't track the 14px eyebrow wider than 0px or bold it past 400 — the uppercase #5c6ae4 already flags it, and extra weight makes it shout over the 64px headline.
- Don't center the shadow at 0px 0px on cards — the 11px 11px offset is the directional signature, and centered glows flatten the paper-on-desk metaphor.
- Never let indigo fill more area than a tag, a checkbox or a selected date — the thesis is an accent that behaves like a cursor, and a large indigo surface erases it.

## Elevation

- **Meeting cards, feature panels, mini calendar and popovers (7 uses):** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) 11px 11px 40px 0px`
- **Hero product window only (1 use):** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2) 0px 1px 128px 0px`

## Imagery

The page uses no photography and no standalone illustration: every image is a product screenshot rebuilt as live interface — calendar windows, meeting documents, slash menus, task pickers — populated with real-sounding teammates (Febby, Augustine, Junnie) and emoji. Windows sit on #ffffff at 24px radius with offset shadows and no borders, cropped by their containers so they bleed off panel edges. Illustrated avatar portraits appear in 32px circles. Icons are small monoline glyphs at 14px inside the mockups. The only illustration-like marks are hand-drawn tick bursts in #5c6ae4 beside feature panels. Gradients are decorative-only fills within 32px panels and card headers, overlaid with grain, not system tokens for page backgrounds. The narrative is a calendar caught mid-meeting by people already using it.

## Layout

Content sits in a 1280px container on a 1920px canvas, with sections separated by 128px rhythm, stretching to 192px before the feature block. The hero is centered: a 14px #5c6ae4 eyebrow, a two-line 64px Walsheim headline with the cursor tag, an 18px three-line paragraph, then a three-window product composition with the main window overlapping its siblings. A 56px centered headline introduces a full-bleed horizontal carousel of four meeting cards. The feature section switches to left-aligned headlines over an asymmetric bento of two to three gradient panels in staggered columns, not the conventional equal three-column grid. There is no pricing grid and no logo row. The nav is sticky, transparent, 48px, wordmark left, avatars right. On phones at 375px, display drops to the 56px step, section gaps tighten to 80px and the bento stacks to one column. Density: spacious.

## Cursor Over Button

The discipline is that Ready's accent behaves like a person in the document rather than a control on a page. Indigo appears as a #5c6ae4 eyebrow, a #7366fe name tag with its 8px 8px 8px 0px pointer corner, a 25%-opacity highlight and checked boxes — every instance is something a collaborator would leave behind. It breaks the moment a designer adds a #7366fe "Get started" pill to the nav or fills a pricing banner with the accent, because the hue stops meaning presence and starts meaning conversion. To extend the system, introduce new accent objects as multiplayer artifacts: a second cursor in #5c6ae4, a comment pin, a typing caret. If a real CTA is required, use the 8px-radius button once per viewport and keep it smaller than the 64px headline.

## Gradient Containment

The dusk palette — #55269c, #7b4096, #8f4d75, #817da6, #6873a5, #6c77b0 — is rich, but it lives only inside rounded containers: 32px feature panels and 24px meeting headers, always with grain and always beside #ffffff UI. The canvas stays #f5f4f1 from top to bottom, which is what lets the gradients read as windows into weather rather than page decoration. Containment breaks with a full-bleed gradient hero, gradient text on headlines, or gradient fills in buttons and charts. Extend it by assigning each new meeting type or feature its own two- or three-stop blend drawn from the six tokens plus a decorative warm corner, keeping the 32px radius, the 48px padding and #ffffff text on top.

## Bold-Then-Quiet Hierarchy

Hierarchy runs on a single cliff: GT Walsheim 700 at 56 and 64px, then nothing until GT America Standard 500 at 24px, then 18, 16 and 14px at 300 to 400. Conventional scales fill that 2.33× gap with 32 and 40px heads, and Ready deliberately does not. The discipline breaks if Walsheim appears below 56px, if America is pushed to 700 for emphasis, or if tracking is introduced on any size. Extend the system by adding content beneath headlines at the existing four text sizes and by using color — #333333 versus #8b8c96 versus #5c6ae4 — for secondary emphasis, keeping every new section opener at 56px Walsheim with 1.0 leading.

## Similar Brands

- **Notion Calendar (Cron)** — the same calendar-as-workspace category and product-screenshot hero, though Cron runs a dark, monochrome canvas where Ready sits on grained #f5f4f1.
- **Amie** — a playful calendar brand pairing rounded geometric display type with soft offset shadows, with more chromatic surfaces than Ready's single indigo accent.
- **Figma** — the multiplayer cursor name tag as a brand device, which Ready adopts as its only accent object.
- **Pitch** — grained gradient feature panels with live collaborative UI embedded inside them, and a similarly restrained neutral canvas around the color.
- **Notion** — block-based documents with emoji headings and slash menus shown as hero proof, with Ready adding heavier geometric headlines and warmer paper.
